findings.reason: with no declared dependency a scheduler can dispatch §3/§4 before the module lands, and the node either blocks or reimplements the metrics, defeating the shared-owner design.
findings.text: §3's done-when reports "link-label AUC ... with its interval" and §4's reports nDCG@10 and review acceptance, both of which need the `sn-judgment-evaluation` evaluation module (`paired_auc`, `bootstrap_interval`, `load_labelled_fixture`), yet neither section declares the depends-on that §2/§5/§6 do; followup f-ssog-001 states the same dependency in prose ("can run as soon as the evaluation module exists").

findings.reason: a node dispatched on §5 without the check source cannot compute the composite it is measured on, the same omission §6's dependency exists to prevent.
findings.text: §5 orders reading by "a Jev risk composite of the named checks most likely to have failed", whose taxonomy and Jev answers are built in `sn-review-through-jev` §2–§3, but §5 declares only `sn-judgment-evaluation#s4` (the goldens), while §6 declares `sn-review-through-jev#s3` for that same feature source.

findings.reason: one node carrying two deliverables cannot be closed on a single verdict, and the prototype's whole purpose (an ear- or-earn-a-node number) is split across two measures.
findings.text: §3 bundles two different judgments — a Noul scoring `name:` link labels (measured by link-label AUC) and a Score ranking family-template anchors (measured by harmonization lint findings) — into one node with two unrelated done-when halves and two evidence outputs.

findings.reason: an unconstrained verdict cannot fail, so the node cannot be shown to have decided anything, unlike §6 which names the rule (beat the hand-set composite by more than its interval).
findings.text: §2's done-when requires the fragment to report exact-name match, per-slot accuracy, family agreement and cost, then "ends with a stated recommendation: cross-check, generator, or neither", but states no threshold or decision rule tying the numbers to the recommendation, so any measured outcome satisfies it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `select_anchor` (`imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:103`), `rerank_pool` (`imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:179`), the `sn-classifier` gpt-5.5 seat (`pyproject.toml:362`), and every cited section (`sn-judgment-evaluation#s3`/`#s4`, `sn-review-through-jev#s3`, `sn-catalog-grouping#s3`/`#s4`, `discovery-judgments-through-jev#s6`) resolve and match their descriptions.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's done-when ends in an unconstrained recommendation ("cross-check, generator, or neither") with no decision rule, so no measurement outcome can falsify it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the sections name evidence fragments and the house convention places them under `docs/evidence/fragments/<plan-slug>/`; no section claims a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the prose names no code symbol, filename or comment after a plan, ticket or version tag; `S19` appears only as plan metadata.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each mechanism is capable of its done-when, the unwired-prototype design is stated as such, and the cited anchors support the claims they are attached to.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §3 carries two independent judgments (link-label classification and family-anchor scoring) under one node with two separate done-when measures.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2, §5 and §6 declare depends-on, but §3 and §4 declare none although both consume the `sn-judgment-evaluation` module, and §5 omits the `sn-review-through-jev` check source that §6 declares for the same feature.
